name: mubit-memory
description: Persistent, typed, self-improving memory for Claude Code, backed by Mubit. Captures work involuntarily, recalls relevant lessons before every prompt, and attributes outcomes so memory improves with use.

endpoint.title: Mubit endpoint
endpoint.description: Your Mubit instance URL, e.g. https://eu.mubit.ai. Required.

apiKey.title: API key
apiKey.description: Mubit API key (mbt_...). Stored in the OS keychain, never in a settings file.

userId.title: User id
userId.description: Optional user/entity id for multi-user memory scoping. This is a retrieval scope, not a name: set it and recall only sees memory captured under the same value.

actorId.title: Actor id
actorId.description: Who captured memory is attributed to. Leave blank and it is detected once per month from github.user, your git commit email or $USER, and recorded as a label on each memory. Unlike userId it never narrows what recall can see.

runStrategy.title: Run strategy
runStrategy.description: How a Claude Code session maps to a Mubit run: per-directory, git-branch, per-conversation, or static.

capture.title: Capture tool activity
capture.description: Capture tool activity into Mubit memory.

recall.title: Inject recalled memory
recall.description: Inject recalled memory before each prompt.

redact.title: Redact before sending
redact.description: Scrub secrets and denylisted paths before anything leaves the machine. Turning this off is not recommended.

recallTokenBudget.title: Recall token budget
recallTokenBudget.description: Maximum tokens of recalled context injected per prompt.

subagentRecallTokenBudget.title: Subagent recall token budget
subagentRecallTokenBudget.description: Maximum tokens of recalled context injected into a subagent when it starts. Kept below recallTokenBudget: a subagent's window is smaller and its task narrower, and this is paid once per spawn, so a fan-out of ten pays it ten times.

recallMaxPerSection.title: Recall items per section
recallMaxPerSection.description: Maximum items rendered per section of the injected block. 0 means no cap, and the token budget is the only limit.

recallAssemble.title: Recall assembly
recallAssemble.description: How recalled memory is assembled: 'client' is free; 'server' uses /v2/control/context, which costs two LLM calls per prompt.

recallRepeatMode.title: Repeated memory
recallRepeatMode.description: What to do with a memory already injected earlier in this run: 'pointer' repeats it as a one-line reference, 'full' re-sends the whole entry on every prompt. Recall injection is the plugin's largest recurring context cost.

recallRankBy.title: Recall ranking
recallRankBy.description: How the server ranks recalled memory: 'auto' reads it off the prompt — a handoff question like 'where were we?' is ranked by recency, everything else by similarity. 'relevance' is the server default and is what made those questions answer with the most similar memory rather than the most recent one; 'freshness' and 'balanced' pin the emphasis for every prompt. Costs nothing: it is one field on a request the plugin already sends. Ignored when recallAssemble is 'server', which has no ranking field at all.

recallAsync.title: Non-blocking recall
recallAsync.description: Never make a prompt wait on recall. The block injected before each prompt is the one retrieved in the background just after the previous prompt, so the hook returns instantly however slow the endpoint is. Costs one turn of staleness, and the first prompt of a session gets no recalled memory.

reflectOnEnd.title: Reflect on session end
reflectOnEnd.description: Reflect when a session ends. This is the only path that promotes a lesson beyond its own run — turning it off costs cross-session memory.

sessionEndDetach.title: Finish the session flush in the background
sessionEndDetach.description: Let the end-of-session drain and reflection finish in a detached process. The host cancels the session-end hook about a second in when a session is torn down, and everything still running inside it dies with it — including the only call that promotes a lesson beyond its own run. Turning this off keeps that work in the hook, where a teardown can cut it short.

outcomeMode.title: Outcome attribution
outcomeMode.description: How turn outcomes are attributed back to recalled memories: off, implicit, or explicit.

statusLine.title: Status line
statusLine.description: Show Mubit connection and capture stats in the status line.

preToolWarnings.title: Warn before matching tool calls
preToolWarnings.description: Show the model a stored Mubit rule just before a matching Bash command runs (rm, git push). It only ever warns: it never blocks, rewrites or asks about a tool call, and it is a memory-informed reminder rather than a security boundary — use permissions for a hard allow or deny. Off by default.

resumeBlock.title: Brief me on where I left off
resumeBlock.description: At the start of a session, assemble a short summary of where earlier work on this project left off and put it in front of your first prompt. It is built in the background, so nothing waits for it, and it costs one round trip and two LLM calls per SESSION rather than per prompt. It is a briefing and not a task list. Only new and resumed sessions get one: /clear starts a fresh run with no history, and a compaction or a fork is already re-anchored.

mcpTools.title: MCP tool allowlist
mcpTools.description: Comma-separated allowlist of Mubit MCP tools. Blank uses the curated default set.

mcpLessonScope.title: MCP lesson scope ceiling
mcpLessonScope.description: The widest scope a lesson written by an MCP tool may claim: run, session, or global. Anything wider than run is read by unrelated runs, so the default keeps an agent's lesson in the run that wrote it; reflection is still the path that promotes one beyond it.
